handNote.desc: Graceful Naskh, calligraphic Naskh, one hand, large

decoDesc.decoNote: The opening pages (ff. 1b-2a) form a symmetrically illuminated double-page frontispiece, such that an analysis of one folio applies to both. Each folio contains a crowned headpiece and a tailpiece both with a horizontal rectangular cartouche positioned directly above and below the main text block. The top cartouche features an anepigraphic central oval medallion flanked by two half-medallions. The bottom cartouche contains an anepigraphic oval medallion at the centre, enclosed within a gilt border filled with arabesque motifs. The crown is a prominent decorative header, featuring a scalloped, dome-like ogival medallion filled with a gilt field of delicate blue, red, and orange floral buds and topped by gilt arabesque motifs. It encloses a smaller ogival medallion at the centre executed in a deep lapis lazuli blue background with gold arabesque motifs. The main dome-like medallion is flanked by two upward cornerpieces in a contrasting palette of gold and minium arabesque motifs on a lapis lazuli blue background. A single decorative panel encloses the two cartouches, rendered in black and sorrounded by a chain-stitch frame in minium. The crowned headpiece features similar ruling on three sides, while at the top a three-line black border replaces the chain-stitch frame. The body text sits on a cream-colored background, enclosed at the bottom, left, and right sides (moving outwardly) by a tick gilt border, a single black ruling, a margin filled with arabesque and Khataʾi floral motifs executed in gilt, lapis lazuli blue, and minium, and finally another thick gilt border. The central text block—containing Sūrat al-Fātiḥah on f. 1b and the first four verses of Sūrat al-Baqarah on f. 2a transcribed in black calligraphic Naskh script—features masterful gilding. Both folios feature intricate arabesque and Khataʾi floral motifs, painted and illuminated in a vibrant palette of lapis lazuli blue, cinnabar, minium, white lead, verdigris, saffron, and indigo.

Within the main body of the text, the titles of the surahs are rubricated, flanked by the remaining words of the previous surah in black, and separated by dividing horizontal lines in cinnabar. The text block is framed by triple-ruled border lines (black, minium, and black moving outwardly). Finally, the layout of the leaves is completed by a single decorative rubricated frame that runs consistently along the outer margins of all subsequent pages.

bindingDesc.p: Lacquer painted in plain gilt with a leather spine, 20 × 29 cm, front + back cover, lacquer painted leather + pasteboard
bindingDesc.decoNote: Three-line border in black ink with gold fill, enclosed by an outer frame of black fretwork.
bindingDesc.condition: The paste-down is damaged, with secondary paper laid over an underlying lacquer painting. The board core shows severe delamination, with its pasteboard layers detached.

history.acquisition: Donated to The Ferdowsi Library by Dr Caro Minasian in 1972.

recordHist.source: This record was created by Dr Mohammad Emami based on the information published in the Persian catalogue by Dr Ali Mir-Ansari (Catalogue of the Persian and Arabic Manuscripts in the Ferdowsi Library, Wadham College, University of Oxford (Minasian Collection), Tehran: Miras-e Maktoob, 2016), with further improvements.

availability.p: Entry to the Library is permitted upon presentation of a valid university ID card (for admissions procedures, please visit Wadham College Library, Persian Studies Section). Please Contact persian.library@wadham.ox.ac.ukfor further information on the availability of this manuscript.
